title: Machine-readable security labeling and releasability at the point of production (born-releasable C2/ISR objects: tracks, reports, video, AI detections)
problem: Tracks, reports, video and AI-derived products are created on U.S. Secret systems without interoperable, machine-enforceable classification/releasability labels (ACP-240/ZTDF/IC-TDF/STANAG 4774-4778), so ABAC engines and cross-domain guards cannot decide automatically and staff regenerate, re-key or hand-carry products to partner enclaves after days-to-weeks of human negotiation.

user.exact_role: Intelligence and fires staff who produce REL products (Army 35F/35G analysts, targeting officers, ISR PED analysts), foreign disclosure officers (FDOs), multinational intelligence cell analysts, cross-domain-solution filter engineers, and data-layer integrators on NGC2/Overmatch/MPE
user.echelon: Division/corps G2 and fires cells, theater/COCOM J2/J3 and JICO cells, coalition CJTF and Mission Partner Environment operators
organization_examples: III Corps / I Corps G2 during Warfighter Exercises (WFX 24-03 documented)
USINDOPACOM J2/J6 and INDOPACOM Mission Network
USEUCOM / NATO Federated Mission Networking nodes
DISA MPE / Coalition Information Environment program office
Joint Staff J6 JDAT (Bold Quest) and NATO CWIX participants

current_workflow: Producer (analyst, sensor operator, AI service) creates a track, report, detection or video clip inside a national system at collateral Secret; the object inherits the system-level classification, not a content-derived label (GAO-25-106454; MIPB WFX 24-03).

A partner needs the product; the release question is negotiated by phone, email and information-exchange requirements between the producer, the FDO and the receiving enclave's administrators (DoD CIO ZT PfMO webinar Sept 2025: 'phone calls, IERs, weeks of negotiation').

The FDO reviews and re-marks by hand against classification guides and disclosure policy; combined or fused objects default to the most restrictive caveat (NOFORN dominates), so the object is often unreleasable as-is.

Staff re-create a sanitized copy on the MPE/REL enclave with a different tool (WFX 24-03: intel regenerated on the lower enclave with REL NATO markings), or move it through an accredited CDS whose static filters reject or quarantine it, or carry it on removable media (INDOPACOM 2024).

Partner receives the product hours to days later, often stripped of provenance; the same negotiation is repeated for the next product type or the next exercise (Balikatan 2026 COP took 'more than eight years' of integration and still depends on JICOs and FDOs).
current_solution: Human FDO review against classification guides; document-centric marking tools (Fortra Titus/Boldon James, Microsoft Purview) that label office files and email but not tactical message objects; accredited CDS guards (Everfox, Owl, GDMS TACDS, Northrop CHORD) with hand-written filters; producing at the lowest classification by policy; DISA MPE lower enclaves and separate coalition networks (CENTRIXS, BICES, Pegasus); commercial unclassified GEOINT as a releasability workaround (NGA Luno); and early data-centric-security stacks (Virtru/OpenTDF ZTDF, Isode and archTIS STANAG 4774/4778 labelers) that are being piloted for enterprise documents and MPE messaging rather than fielded for machine-generated C2/ISR objects.
failure: Labels are absent or system-inherited at the moment of creation; there is no controlled vocabulary shared across mission domains so machine rules cannot interoperate; fused/aggregated objects cannot compute a dominance-aware releasability set, so the most-restrictive caveat wins; every new automated release path needs NSA/NCDSMO-style accreditation; and disclosure authority remains a human decision by regulation, so even where a format (ZTDF/ACP-240) exists, the producer-side derivation of the label for tracks, CoT, detections and video is still manual or missing.

evidence.claim: GAO found 'overly restrictive data classification' is 'a significant hindrance to sharing command and control data' with allies and across services, and officials were not aware of any DoD entity working on a solution; DoD mostly concurred with the recommendations.
evidence.source_title: GAO-25-106454, Defense Command and Control: Further Progress Hinges on Establishing a Comprehensive Framework
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: During Warfighter Exercise 24-03, intelligence produced at collateral Secret could not be shared with allies and had to be regenerated on the MPE lower enclave with REL NATO markings using a different tool; BICES did not communicate with mission command systems.
evidence.source_title: Military Intelligence Professional Bulletin, 'Multinational Intelligence Sharing' (Continuous Transformation 2025 issue)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD CIO Zero Trust PfMO subject-matter expert described current cross-domain tagging coordination as 'phone calls, IERs, weeks of negotiation' with incompatible local definitions and named ZTDF/ABAC and a controlled vocabulary as the target; the ZT target-level deadline is 30 Sept 2027.
evidence.source_title: DoD CIO Zero Trust PfMO / DAU webinar 'Interoperable Data Tagging' (J. Gottlieb), mirrored transcript
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The director of DoD's Zero Trust PfMO (Randy Resnick) said data tagging and labeling is a 'big hurdle' to reaching the FY2027 target and that DoD is running pilots (18 pilots, about 20 vendors) to arrive at a standard approach to data tags and labels - i.e., the problem is acknowledged but unsolved at the department level.
evidence.source_title: MeriTalk, 'DoD Running Data Tagging Pilots to Address Zero Trust Pillar'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Balikatan 2026 fielded the first eight-nation common operating picture after 'more than eight years' of integration work, and the flow still depends on JICOs and foreign-disclosure officers - release remains a human bottleneck even in the flagship coalition exercise.
evidence.source_title: DVIDS, 'Balikatan 2026 debuts groundbreaking common operating picture'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: INDOPACOM Mission Network officials said partner data still moved by 'thumb drives or CDs, or sometimes people looking at two different monitors' and that even after consolidation 'you can't send an attachment' to some allies for lack of data-sharing policy.
evidence.source_title: Defense One, 'INDOPACOM is replacing a pile of partner-nation networks with just one'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DEVCOM C5ISR Center issued the 'Tactical Data in Use Security' (DUCES) RFI surveying industry for DoD Zero Trust Data-Pillar capabilities that must operate inside DDIL tactical networks; the deadline was later extended - a direct government statement that tactical object-level data protection (which presupposes machine-readable labels) is not available today.
evidence.source_title: Breaking Defense, 'Army says DUCES to cyber hackers: New RFI looks for tactical edge zero trust solutions'; SAM.gov notice 784528d45bcc4bcaa163a33e6562bef2
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NAVWAR open SBIR topic 'Data Integrity and Control in DDIL Environments' asks for data protected as an object independent of network or application using ICDF/ZTDF formats that function in DDIL conditions and recover on reconnection - a service-level solicitation for exactly the born-labeled object model.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Joint Staff J6 FY2027 RDT&E justification lists ACP-240, ICAM and Zero Trust as coalition 'testing standards' and continues demonstrating data-centric security for partners beyond FVEY (Bold Quest-type events) - funding exists for demonstration and assessment, not for a production labeling product.
evidence.source_title: FY2027 President's Budget, The Joint Staff RDT&E justification (C5 capability development / JOTG lines)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ACP-240 (CCEB data-centric security publication built on ZTDF) was reported adopted by FVEY and other allied nations in Oct 2025; Everfox and Virtru announced a partnership (16 Oct 2025) to pair ZTDF labeling with accredited cross-domain guards; NSA's Zero Trust Implementation Guideline Phase Two (Apr 2026) references ZTDF/IC-TDF for data rights management. The format/wrapper layer is therefore being claimed by incumbents; the producer-side derivation of labels for tactical objects is not evidenced as solved.
evidence.source_title: BusinessWire, 'Everfox and Virtru Partner to Improve Zero Trust Interoperability Among National Security Agencies'; Virtru newsroom on ACP 240 adoption; GlobeNewswire on NSA ZT guideline
evidence.label: FACT (announcements are vendor-issued; adoption scope and deployment status are INFERENCE)

evidence.claim: Releasability markings do not aggregate by dominance: any NOFORN element in a combined object blocks release to all foreign nationals, so guards must apply the most restrictive constraint and fused C2/ISR products become unreleasable - existing labelers and guards enforce this but do not compute a releasable subset at creation time.
evidence.source_title: Anchor Defense, 'Cross Domain Solution Cross-Tagging and Attribution Controls for Multi-Level Data Release' and 'Cross Domain Solution Data Labeling and Marking Automation for Mission Systems'
evidence.label: FACT (policy rule) / INFERENCE (operational impact)

evidence.claim: DISA says the Mission Partner Environment remains network-centric and will move to data-centric with zero trust by about early 2027, 'starting small' with Indo-Pacific proof-outs - the buyer's own timeline confirms object-level labeling is not yet operational in the coalition environment.
evidence.source_title: Federal News Network, 'DISA starting small in proving out Mission Partner Environment capabilities'
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The format layer has been taken by standards-body-backed vendors: Virtru stewards OpenTDF/ZTDF and now markets ACP-240 conformance with Everfox's accredited guards (Oct 2025), Isode and archTIS sell STANAG 4774/4778 labelers for FMN messaging, and XQ Message claims ACP-240 delivery. None of them, on public evidence, derives labels from the content and provenance of machine-generated tactical objects (CoT/VMF/Link-16 J-series tracks, STANAG 4676 tracks, AI detections, FMV clips) or computes dominance-aware releasable subsets at creation time, because (a) that requires access to classified security classification guides and FDO policy that a startup cannot obtain without a sponsor; (b) the buyers (DoD CIO ZT PfMO, DISA MPE, Joint Staff J6) have treated tagging as a pilot-and-demonstration activity (18 pilots, Bold Quest 'testing standards') rather than a funded product line; (c) every automated release path must pass NSA/NCDSMO-style assessment, which exceeds startup runway; and (d) the C2 message schemas are niche and controlled by program offices and standards bodies, so a labeler needs integration rights that only NGC2/Overmatch/MPE integrators hold.
technical_wedge: A 'label compiler' for machine-generated C2/ISR objects: a rules engine and SDK that ingests tactical message streams (CoT, VMF/MIL-STD-2045, Link-16 J-series via JREAP, STANAG 4676 tracks, NVG overlays, AI detection JSON, KLV-tagged FMV segments), derives a STANAG 4774 confidentiality label from schema fields, source attributes and a declarative policy (sensor type, geography, source nationality, aggregation rules), emits ACP-240/ZTDF or IC-TDF assertions via the OpenTDF SDK, computes per-partner releasability sets with dominance-aware aggregation, and produces (i) CDS-filter-ready metadata for Everfox/Owl/GDMS guards and (ii) an auditable 'would this pass' simulator plus conformance linter for exercise data. The startup owns the derivation rules, schema bindings and the audit/explanation layer; it does not own the wrapper (OpenTDF), the guard (CDS incumbents) or the release authority (FDO).

mvp.what: Open-source conformance linter and rules engine that takes synthetic CoT/VMF/STANAG 4676 feeds and AI-detection outputs, attaches STANAG 4774 labels bound per STANAG 4778, wraps them as ZTDF using OpenTDF, computes releasable subsets for a configurable partner matrix (e.g., REL FVEY, REL NATO, NOFORN), and shows FDO review time saved on a simulated coalition COP.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for an unclassified demo: TAK Server plug-in that labels CoT objects at ingest, a policy console for the partner matrix, an audit log, and an open-source guard-simulation (e.g., NiFi with Owl's open DFDL schemas) showing which objects pass to a simulated MPE enclave; measurable metrics: fraction of objects auto-labeled, false-release rate against a hand-marked test set, time to produce a REL subset.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That labels derived by rules from message content and provenance match human FDO decisions on an unclassified test corpus at a false-release rate low enough for a disclosure authority to accept machine pre-decisions (human-on-the-loop), that the output is consumable by at least one accredited guard's filter format and one ABAC engine, and that dominance-aware aggregation yields materially more releasable objects than system-level inheritance.

data_requirement.what: Public marking policy (DoDM 5200.01 volumes, CAPCO/ISM register, DoDM 5230.09 disclosure policy at the unclassified level), STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 specifications, OpenTDF/ZTDF schemas, C2 message schemas (CoT, MIL-STD-2045/VMF via Owl's public DFDL schemas, STANAG 4676, NVG), synthetic tactical message corpora, and later a sponsor-provided hand-marked unclassified or CUI exercise corpus; real security classification guides and REL decisions are classified or CUI and require a government sponsor.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Partially. Specifications and open schemas are obtainable (ACP-240 Ed A text availability should be verified; some CCEB/NATO documents are limited distribution). Synthetic corpora can be generated. Hand-marked real exercise data is CUI or classified and available only under a sponsor agreement; export-controlled CUI is effectively U.S.-person-only, so the Indonesian founder could not handle it - needs counsel.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; the German founder qualifies only after obtaining permanent residency, and the Indonesian founder's equity would count against the ownership test - the cap table must be structured with counsel. Neither Germany nor Indonesia is a 'foreign country of concern' for the SBIR foreign-disclosure form (E07-F4), but foreign affiliations must be disclosed. Any work touching classification guides, REL decisions or export-controlled CUI is effectively U.S.-person-only (E07-F30) and the DDTC/ITAR question (labeling of defense-article data is likely not itself a defense article, but the surrounding data may be) needs export-control counsel; a FOCI mitigation may be triggered even on unclassified contracts (DoDI 5205.87, E07-F20). Do not treat these as settled - obtain counsel before incorporation.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes for their own platforms: Palantir and Anduril already enforce markings inside their data layers and could emit ZTDF via OpenTDF in a quarter; Everfox+Virtru have publicly assembled the label+guard stack (Oct 2025); L3Harris/GDMS/Owl control the guard filters. What they are structurally poor at is a cross-vendor, standards-based derivation layer that works identically across Lattice, Maven, SitaWare and TAK - each incumbent prefers labels bound to its own object model.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Conditional win: the only defensible position is the neutral 'label compiler' plus conformance/audit tooling that program offices and JITC/CWIX can use to test every vendor's output, sold first to exercise and integrator budgets. If DoD instead mandates a single vendor format and buys labeling inside NGC2/MPE integrator contracts, or if FDO policy never accepts machine pre-decisions, the startup is reduced to a feature. For this specific team (one non-U.S.-person founder, no classified access) the odds tilt toward reject unless the company is built around the NATO/FMN allied profile first.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The product sits on classification policy (human disclosure authority by regulation), NSA/NCDSMO cross-domain assessment for any automated release path (NIST AC-4(20) restricts to approved CDS), DoD ZT/RMF authorization (SWFT/cATO evidence), CUI and export-control handling of marking guides and exercise data, and possible FOCI mitigation. The unclassified conformance-tooling wedge lowers the burden for the first 12-18 months but every step toward real REL decisions raises it sharply.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a U.S. person) cannot lawfully access export-controlled CUI, classified marking guides or most sponsor exercise data, and would count against SBIR U.S.-ownership thresholds; the German founder needs permanent residency before SBIR eligibility and a clearance path. This is a direct conflict with the mission of the product, not a peripheral issue: the company would need a U.S.-person-only technical enclave and possibly a mitigated structure. Describe constraints only - requires immigration, export-control and FOCI counsel; no legal judgment made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Attribute-based labeling and releasability computation for structured, machine-generated data has analogues in regulated data sharing (health, financial, critical infrastructure OT telemetry, multi-party industrial consortia), and the OpenTDF ecosystem is commercial. However, the dominance-aware military marking logic and coalition partner matrices are defense-specific; a commercial pivot would be a different product on the same engine. Allied/NATO defense is the more realistic 'second market' than commercial.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility comes from (1) validated derivation rule sets and hand-marked test corpora that show agreement with FDO decisions (data + algorithms), (2) bindings to each message schema and each guard's filter format (integrations), (3) any assessment/accreditation artifacts that let an automated path be reused across programs (accreditation), and (4) being the conformance tool used at CWIX/Bold Quest/JITC (workflow and relationships). The wrapper itself (OpenTDF) is open and not defensible; if the startup only builds a ZTDF emitter it has nothing.

why_now: Three things changed in 2023-2026: (1) the standards converged - ZTDF was ratified through the CCEB and ACP-240 was reported adopted by FVEY and other allies in Oct 2025, ACP-240 supplements were aligned with STANAG 4774/4778, and NSA's ZT Implementation Guideline Phase Two (Apr 2026) named ZTDF/IC-TDF, so for the first time a producer can emit one label that U.S., FVEY and NATO systems are supposed to consume; (2) the deadlines arrived - DoD ZT target level by 30 Sept 2027 with data tagging publicly called the biggest hurdle, DISA moving MPE to data-centric by early 2027, and Maven made the CJADC2 cornerstone (Mar-Apr 2026) with coalition users; (3) the object volume exploded - NGC2 declared ready to scale with 60+ vendors on a common data layer (Jul 2026), AI detections and AI-enabled coalition exercises (Talisman Sabre 2025, Balikatan 2026) generate machine products faster than FDOs can review, making producer-side labeling a throughput problem rather than a policy nicety. Labels: FACT for the standards and deadlines (MEDIUM, partly vendor-reported), INFERENCE for the volume argument.
killer_risk: Disclosure is a legally human decision and the buyers have kept tagging in the pilot-and-demonstration circuit for five years (18 ZT pilots, Bold Quest 'testing standards', 14% of ZT target activities complete in early 2025); meanwhile the format layer is now owned by Virtru/OpenTDF with Everfox's guards, and Palantir/Anduril will label inside their own data layers - so the remaining 'label compiler' niche may be too small and too policy-gated to fund a company, and this particular team cannot legally touch the data that would make the rules real. INFERENCE, MEDIUM-HIGH.

allied_extension: Yes, materially. NATO already has the label standards (STANAG 4774/4778) baked into Federated Mission Networking profiles and tests conformance annually at CWIX, ACP-240 now bridges those to ZTDF, and European nations (Bundeswehr, Nordic and Baltic FMN affiliates) buy from smaller vendors (Isode, archTIS, Systematic partners) with lower accreditation walls than NSA/NCDSMO. The German founder can pursue NATO DIANA, Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub and FMN spiral participation without the U.S.-person problem, and a NATO-first conformance tool could later be brought into U.S. coalition programs (MPE/CIE) as the 'allied-proven' labeler. Caveat: European budgets for this niche are small and fragmented by nation, and NATO's own timelines (ACCS took two decades) are slow - INFERENCE, MEDIUM.
